claim: Descriptive complete-file tail stereo; no width fit or hardware equivalence claim.
latency_compensation: Production only: exactly93samples; hardware unshifted. Different excitation histories are not time aligned.
guard_policy: Exploratory descriptive flags: RMS>=−65dBFS, second-half RMS rise<=1dB, half-window normalized octave-power cosine>=.90. These are neither perceptual thresholds nor a proof that no new notes occurred. All windows retained; exclude visibly edited endings beyond the chosen ranges.
source_inspection: Last obvious new pitch/excitation ranges are coarse manual spectrogram/RMS observations, not recovered MIDI. Hardware analysis begins>=1s after latest possible obvious note onset; first Air window is only.5s after the conservative excitation upper bound and is labeled sensitivity.
channel_sensitivity: Cotton only: divide right channel by10^(.6/20), fixed from early recording imbalance; does not change DSP. Air early excerpt is already wet and supplies no clean capture-gain estimate.
coherence: Power-weighted per-bin magnitude-squared coherence,18overlapping4096sampleHannSTFTframes per0.5swindow. Not independent trials; no confidence intervals. Very weak bands are retained without a hardware interpretation.

Velocity 100 is a placeholder for every note; original velocity, controllers, system transpose and exact recording patch revision are unverified.
Published delay/reverb and recording processing obscure exact key-down/up times. Note boundaries are estimated, generally within 10–30 ms; longer ambiguity is described below.
No Septum audio or synthesis parameter search was used to choose these notes. The paired Roland preset must remain unmodified.
The continuous melodic line, short portamento and active pitch modulation leave exact articulation and overlap unknown; adjacent notes use adjoining estimated gates.
The 3.45-second prefix intentionally stops during the final note; its final note-off at 3.445 seconds is an artificial crop boundary, not a measured hardware key release.

This is an estimated reconstruction, not a recovered original MIDI performance.
Played MIDI octave is conditional on the measured WIDE-off range and default system transpose. The original performance MIDI has not been recovered.
Bass C2/C3 octave allocation is less certain than the Eb/F/Bb and Eb/F/A chord pitch classes because their harmonics overlap.
Onsets are approximate within roughly30–70 ms, with the later F3 strum less certain. Short-time analysis window smears exact attacks.
Note-off times are placeholders informed by audible-band decay; release envelopes and reverb prevent exact recovery.
Velocities, controllers, pitch bend, system transpose/tuning, master gain, and recording processing are unknown.
Small note overlaps, extra quiet notes, and the exact voicing may differ from this estimate.

All note-on velocities fixed to100 as an explicit placeholder. Original velocities were not recoverable, and filter velocity sensitivity is+18 in the published patch. No velocity or preset parameters were fitted against Septum output.
Five-second excerpt only; the later untranscribed performance is not compared with the rendered release tail.
